--- a/minbpe/regex.py
+++ b/minbpe/regex.py
@@ -44,17 +44,26 @@
-        ids = [list(ch.encode("utf-8")) for ch in text_chunks]
-
-        # iteratively merge the most common pairs to create new tokens
-        merges = {} # (int, int) -> int
-        vocab = {idx: bytes([idx]) for idx in range(256)} # idx -> bytes
-        for i in range(num_merges):
-            # count the number of times every consecutive pair appears
-            stats = {}
-            for chunk_ids in ids:
-                # passing in stats will update it in place, adding up counts
-                get_stats(chunk_ids, stats)
-            # find the pair with the highest count
-            pair = max(stats, key=stats.get)
-            # mint a new token: assign it the next available id
-            idx = 256 + i
-            # replace all occurrences of pair in ids with idx
-            ids = [merge(chunk_ids, pair, idx) for chunk_ids in ids]
+        # identical chunks are deduplicated (first-occurrence order kept) and
+        # weighted by their frequency; this yields identical pair counts and
+        # identical stats insertion order (hence identical tie-breaking)
+        chunk_counts = {}
+        for ch in text_chunks:
+            chunk_counts[ch] = chunk_counts.get(ch, 0) + 1
+        ids = [list(ch.encode("utf-8")) for ch in chunk_counts]
+        freqs = list(chunk_counts.values())
+
+        # iteratively merge the most common pairs to create new tokens
+        merges = {} # (int, int) -> int
+        vocab = {idx: bytes([idx]) for idx in range(256)} # idx -> bytes
+        for i in range(num_merges):
+            # count the number of times every consecutive pair appears
+            stats = {}
+            get = stats.get
+            for chunk_ids, f in zip(ids, freqs):
+                for p in zip(chunk_ids, chunk_ids[1:]):
+                    stats[p] = get(p, 0) + f
+            # find the pair with the highest count
+            pair = max(stats, key=stats.get)
+            # mint a new token: assign it the next available id
+            idx = 256 + i
+            # replace all occurrences of pair in ids with idx
+            p0, p1 = pair
+            ids = [merge(c, pair, idx) if p0 in c and len(c) > 1 else c for c in ids]

actions.reason: RegexTokenizer.train now deduplicates identical regex chunks, keeping them in first-occurrence order, and weights each unique chunk by its frequency. Pair counts come out the same, and pairs enter the stats dict in the same order, so max() breaks ties the same way and the merges are identical. Merging skips chunks that cannot contain the pair. Measured train_regex_ir ratio is 0.365, the equivalence check gave identical outputs, and the other metrics are unchanged.

diff --git a/minbpe/regex.py b/minbpe/regex.py
--- a/minbpe/regex.py
+++ b/minbpe/regex.py
@@ -41,7 +41,14 @@ class RegexTokenizer(Tokenizer):
         text_chunks = re.findall(self.compiled_pattern, text)
 
         # input text preprocessing
-        ids = [list(ch.encode("utf-8")) for ch in text_chunks]
+        # identical chunks are deduplicated (first-occurrence order kept) and
+        # weighted by their frequency; this yields identical pair counts and
+        # identical stats insertion order (hence identical tie-breaking)
+        chunk_counts = {}
+        for ch in text_chunks:
+            chunk_counts[ch] = chunk_counts.get(ch, 0) + 1
+        ids = [list(ch.encode("utf-8")) for ch in chunk_counts]
+        freqs = list(chunk_counts.values())
 
         # iteratively merge the most common pairs to create new tokens
         merges = {} # (int, int) -> int
@@ -49,15 +56,17 @@ class RegexTokenizer(Tokenizer):
         for i in range(num_merges):
             # count the number of times every consecutive pair appears
             stats = {}
-            for chunk_ids in ids:
-                # passing in stats will update it in place, adding up counts
-                get_stats(chunk_ids, stats)
+            get = stats.get
+            for chunk_ids, f in zip(ids, freqs):
+                for p in zip(chunk_ids, chunk_ids[1:]):
+                    stats[p] = get(p, 0) + f
             # find the pair with the highest count
             pair = max(stats, key=stats.get)
             # mint a new token: assign it the next available id
             idx = 256 + i
             # replace all occurrences of pair in ids with idx
-            ids = [merge(chunk_ids, pair, idx) for chunk_ids in ids]
+            p0, p1 = pair
+            ids = [merge(c, pair, idx) if p0 in c and len(c) > 1 else c for c in ids]
             # save the merge
             merges[pair] = idx
             vocab[idx] = vocab[pair[0]] + vocab[pair[1]]

journal.text:
I read minbpe/regex.py and the top of base.py, then rewrote lines 44-60 of regex.py so RegexTokenizer.train deduplicates identical regex chunks in first-occurrence order and weights each unique chunk by its count. Pairs enter the stats dict in the same order, so max() ties break the same way. The merge step also skips chunks that cannot contain the pair.

My sandbox run on train_regex_ir was accepted with identical outputs. train_regex_ir went from 6815654494 to 2486948482, ratio 0.3649. The other metrics barely moved: train_basic_ir 1.0008, encode_ir 1.0002, decode_ir 1.0000, save_load_ir 0.9999. Guard was ok with 1 file and 19 lines. I submitted it and it is queued for replay. No verdict yet.

Most of the regex training cost came from recounting duplicate chunks. Keeping insertion order is what keeps the merges identical.

Next I would look at encode_ir, maybe caching per-chunk encodings, and check whether basic training can use a similar skip in merge.
